construction_markdown:
No new leaderboard construction is claimed. This turn closes and normalizes the standard cyclic/BCH architectures.

Fix `F=F_2[T]/(T^30+T+1)`, `q=|F|=2^30`, and `theta=T mod (T^30+T+1)`. For odd `d`, define

`C_d={ (b+Tr(sum_{j odd, 1<=j<=d} a_j x^j))_{x in F} : b in F_2, a_j in F }`.

The proved anchor `C_65` has parameters `[2^30,991,535822336]_2`; it is not resubmitted because the shared campaign already has a stronger dimension-1040 RS–affine construction. The conditional frontier `C_69` has exact dimension 1051 and a fully explicit generator matrix, but its distance is not proved: ordinary Hasse–Weil gives only `535756800`.

Two additional exact closures are proved. First, the largest target-safe binary cyclic code of exact length `2^30` has dimension exactly 3. Second, the parity-extended primitive narrow-sense BCH construction whose distance is certified only by its consecutive roots has maximum dimension 236 at the target.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: lemma editor and algebraic integrator. For `N=2^m`, every binary cyclic code is the chain ideal `<(X+1)^(N-k)>` in `F_2[X]/((X+1)^N)`. If `k>=4`, it contains `(X+1)^(N-4)`, of weight `N/4`. The `k=3` ideal has basis exponents `N-3,N-2,N-1`; Lucas' theorem shows that its seven nonzero words have weights `N/2` or `N`. Thus the maximum cyclic dimension at the immutable target is exactly 3, not merely at most 3.
discussion_posts.subject: Exact repeated-root cyclic optimum

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: degree-69 bottleneck breaker. Put `M(a,b)=max_{P in L_65}|S(P+aX^67+bX^69)|`. Under `(a,b)->(a u^67,b u^69)`, `M` is invariant. Since `gcd(67,2^30-1)=1` and `gcd(69,2^30-1)=3`, the nonzero coefficient pairs have exactly `2^30+3` orbits: representatives `(1,beta)` for every `beta in F`, and `(0,gamma)` for the three cubic classes. One may normalize with `67^(-1)=849377860 mod (2^30-1)`. Translation preserves the top pair after trace reduction. This is the smallest exact affine-normal-form ledger for attacking the universal bound.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: Intended recipient: algebraic bottleneck and literature positions. The checked refinements do not certify `C_69`: Voloch's improved theorem requires `t>2^14`, whereas designed distance 71 has `t=35`; Férard's specialized improvement concerns top degree `2^a-1`, not 69; and the Scholten–Zhu nonsupersingularity theorem concerns genus `2^r-1`, not genus 34. Please either prove `|S(f)|<=64·2^15` for every reduced odd `deg(f)<=69`, or exhibit one explicit violating phase. By the weighted-orbit dichotomy, a counterexample closes every dimension-at-least-1041 extension using only the 67/69 layers.

distance_audit: The immutable distance is `D=2^29-2^20=535822336`. For a trace family containing the external constant, the equivalent signed-sum requirement is `|S(f)|<=q-2D=2^21=64·2^15`.
The exact-length cyclic ideal of dimension 3 has minimum distance `q/2=536870912>D`. Every cyclic ideal of dimension at least 4 contains a word of weight `q/4=268435456<D`.
For the full-field BCH/subfield-subcode polynomial cutoff `B=q-D=537919488`, every nonzero representative has at most `B` roots, so its binary evaluation has weight at least `q-B=D`.

For every nonzero reduced odd polynomial of degree at most 65, the Artin–Schreier curve has genus at most 32. Hasse–Weil therefore gives `|S|<=64·2^15`, covering every nonzero word of `C_65`; the constant-only word has weight `q`.
Férard's attainment theorem at designed distance `67=2^6+3` supplies a degree-at-most-65 trace word with weight deviation exactly `2^20`. Hence `d_min(C_65)=D`, not just `>=D`.
The generic degree-67 certificate gives only `d>=2^29-33·2^15=535789568`, short by 32768.
The generic degree-69 certificate gives only `d>=2^29-34·2^15=535756800`, short by 65536. No target-distance claim is made for `C_69`.
For `C(V)=C_65+{Tr(aX^67+bX^69):(a,b) in V}`, target distance is equivalent to the absolute signed-sum cap for every nonconstant phase because the external constant supplies every complement.
explicitness_audit: The field is the fixed quotient `F_2[T]/(T^30+T+1)`; the accepted Rabin certificate in `algebraic-04.json` proves irreducibility.
Columns are all 30-bit polynomial-basis field elements in increasing integer order. Rows are ordered first by exponent and then by the basis coefficients `1,theta,...,theta^29`.
The proved `C_65` matrix consists of the all-one row and 990 rows `Tr(theta^i x^j)` for odd `j<=65`. The conditional `C_69` matrix appends the analogous 60 rows for `j=67,69`.
The complete matrices are streamed deterministically in `O(k n (log n)^3)` bit operations. No sampling, selector, exhaustive construction search, padding, or hidden coordinate ordering is involved.
The `q+3` orbit classification and the upstream 5,995,866-mask codimension-10 check are proof reductions; neither selects a generator matrix.
Explicitness is not the obstruction for `C_69`; the sole missing item is a universal distance proof.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Represent `F` in the polynomial basis `1,theta,...,theta^29` and enumerate columns by integers `0,...,2^30-1`, interpreted as coefficient bitmasks. Emit row 0 as all ones. For every odd `j=1,3,...,69` and `i=0,...,29`, emit entry `Tr_(F/F_2)(theta^i x^j)` in column `x`. This outputs the complete `1051 by 2^30` matrix of the conditional degree-69 code. Restricting to `j<=65` outputs the proved `991 by 2^30` anchor.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: `O(k n (log n)^3)` bit operations and `O(log n)` working bits beyond streamed output; in particular at most `O(n^2(log n)^3)`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: Let `m=log_2 n=30`. Naive multiplication modulo the fixed degree-`m` polynomial costs `O(m^2)` bit operations. Binary powering to an exponent at most 69 and computing the absolute trace using `m-1` Frobenius squarings cost `O(m^3)` per matrix entry under a conservative accounting. There are exactly `k n` entries and `k<=1051<=n`, proving the stated deterministic polynomial bound.

proof_markdown:
## 1. Target normalization

Put `q=2^30` and `s=sqrt(q)=2^15`. For a Boolean trace phase `f`, let `S(f)=sum_x (-1)^f(x)`. Its truth-table weight is `(q-S(f))/2`. Since every `C_d` contains the external constant, it contains both a phase and its complement. Therefore its target distance is equivalent to

`|S(f)|<=q-2D=2^21=64s`

for every nonconstant phase.

## 2. Exact classification of length-q cyclic codes

In characteristic two,

`X^q-1=(X+1)^q`.

Writing `Y=X+1`, every ideal of `F_2[X]/(X^q-1)=F_2[Y]/(Y^q)` is `<Y^(q-k)>` and has dimension `k`. If `k>=4`, the ideal contains `Y^(q-4)`. Lucas' theorem gives

`wt((1+X)^e)=2^wt_2(e)`.

The binary expansion of `q-4` has 28 ones, so `Y^(q-4)` has weight `2^28<D`. Hence `k<=3`.

For `k=3`, use the basis `A=Y^(q-3)`, `B=Y^(q-2)`, and `J=Y^(q-1)`. Lucas' theorem identifies their supports as

`A={i: bit_1(i)=0}`, `B={i: bit_0(i)=0}`, and `J={0,...,q-1}`.

Thus `A`, `B`, `A+B`, their complements by `J`, and `A+B+J` all have weight `q/2`; `J` has weight `q`. Every nonzero word therefore has weight at least `q/2`. The exact cyclic optimum is `[q,3,q/2]_2`.

## 3. The designed-root BCH route

Let `Q=q-1` and `B=q-D=2^29+2^20`. Consider

`S_B=ev_F({f in F[X]:deg(f)<=B}) intersect F_2^q`.

A function of degree below `q` is binary-valued exactly when `f^2=f mod (X^q-X)`. For positive exponents this makes its support a union of complete doubling orbits modulo `Q`; an orbit of size `r` contributes exactly `r` binary dimensions through its coefficient field `F_(2^r)`. Thus

`dim(S_B)=1+sum_(O contained in [1,B]) |O|`.

Doubling modulo `Q` cyclically rotates the 30-bit exponent word. Requiring every rotation to be at most `2^29+2^20` permits the weight-one orbit; weight-two separations 9 through 15; and the unique weight-three necklace with gaps `10,10,10`. The corresponding orbit sizes are seven copies of 30, then 15 and 10. Hence

`dim(S_B)=1+7·30+15+10=236`.

Every nonzero representing polynomial has at most `B` roots, so its evaluation has weight at least `q-B=D`. On `F*`, Fourier duality identifies the punctured code with the primitive narrow-sense BCH code of designed distance `D-1`; the `x=0` coordinate is its parity extension. A smaller designed distance cannot certify `D` after adding one parity coordinate, so 236 is the exact maximum within this consecutive-root certificate.

## 4. Dual-BCH trace codes

For odd `d<=69`, `C_d` is binary linear and has exact length `q`. A nonzero odd polynomial of degree `e` defines the Artin–Schreier curve

`Y^2+Y=P(X)`

of genus `(e-1)/2`. Hasse–Weil gives

`|S(P)|<=(e-1)s`.

This bound is strictly below `q` for `e<=69`, so no nonzero parameter tuple evaluates to a constant phase. The evaluation map is injective and

`dim(C_d)=1+30(d+1)/2`.

For `d=65`, the signed-sum cap is exactly `64s`, giving `k=991` and `d_min>=D`. Férard's Theorem 1.1(ii), applied with extension degree 30 and `a=6`, states that the Carlitz–Uchiyama bound is attained at designed distance `2^6+3=67`. Its punctured word has weight deviation `64·2^14=2^20`; the zero coordinate does not alter its weight. Thus `d_min(C_65)=D` exactly.

For degrees 67 and 69, the same calculation gives dimensions 1021 and 1051 but only signed-sum caps `66s` and `68s`, respectively. These yield the sub-target lower bounds recorded in the parameter ledger.

## 5. New affine normal form for the terminal layers

Let `L_65` be the odd coefficient space through degree 65 and define

`M(a,b)=max_(P in L_65)|sum_(x in F)(-1)^Tr(P(x)+a x^67+b x^69)|`.

Substitution `x=uy` shows

`M(a,b)=M(a u^67,b u^69)`.

Now `gcd(67,q-1)=1`, while `gcd(69,q-1)=3`. If `a!=0`, put `r=849377860`, for which `67r=1 mod (q-1)`, and take `u=a^(-r)`. This gives the unique representative `(1,b a^(-69r))`; consequently there are exactly `q` orbits with first coordinate nonzero. If `a=0,b!=0`, the orbits are the three cubic classes of `F*`. There are therefore exactly `q+3` nonzero weighted-scaling orbits.

Translations introduce no new degree-67 or degree-69 coefficient. Indeed, Lucas' theorem shows that the odd exponents below 69 occurring in `(X+t)^69` are `1,5,65`, and those below 67 occurring in `(X+t)^67` are `1,3,65`; even exponents reduce to lower odd exponents under `Tr(z^2)=Tr(z)`. Constants disappear under the absolute value. Hence affine changes preserve the displayed top-pair normal form.

## 6. All-or-nothing extension theorem

For `V<=F^2`, set

`C(V)=C_65+{(Tr(a x^67+b x^69))_(x in F):(a,b) in V}`.

Injectivity gives `dim(C(V))=991+dim(V)`. Beating the shared dimension-1040 endpoint requires `dim(V)>=50`, equivalently codimension at most 10.

The upstream weighted-orbit lemma proves that every such `V` meets every orbit `(a u^67,b u^69)`. For codimension at most 9 this follows from Chevalley–Warning applied to at most nine cubic equations in 30 variables. At codimension 10, the possible parity obstruction reduces to exact covers of `Z/30` by ten translates of `{0,1,6}` or `{0,2,6}`. The fixed mask computation checks 5,995,866 cases and obtains maxima `20,23,26`, below the required `22,25,28`, excluding every cover.

Safety is constant on a weighted orbit by the scaling identity for `M`. Therefore a target-safe `V` of dimension at least 50 exists if and only if the full `V=F^2` is safe. In the positive case the result is the explicit dimension-1051 code `C_69`; a single violating phase rules out every such selector. This equivalence is proved, but neither outcome of the character-sum decision is presently established.

## 7. Literature and explicitness conclusion

The checked specialized theorems do not close the remaining `4s` gap. Voloch's improved range begins at `t>2^14`, whereas here `t=35`. Férard's degree-specific improvement is for degree `2^a-1`, and Scholten–Zhu's nonsupersingularity theorem concerns genus `2^r-1`; neither covers degree 69 and genus 34.

The complete `C_69` generator is nevertheless deterministic and polynomial-time, as specified in `generator_matrix`. Thus the terminal obstruction is purely the universal distance inequality, not construction explicitness.

theorem_statement: At `n=2^30` and `D=535822336`: (i) the maximum target-safe dimension among exact-length binary cyclic codes is exactly 3; (ii) the parity-extended primitive narrow-sense BCH construction certified only by consecutive roots has maximum dimension 236; (iii) the generic Carlitz–Uchiyama/Artin–Schreier trace certificate is sharply attained by the exact `[2^30,991,D]_2` degree-65 code; and (iv) every degree-67/69 coefficient selector large enough to beat the shared dimension-1040 endpoint is safe if and only if the full explicit dimension-1051 degree-69 code is safe. The latter distance statement remains unresolved. The degree-69 top coefficient pairs reduce to exactly `2^30+3` nonzero weighted-scaling normal forms.
